prompt: How must an ammeter be connected to measure the current through a resistor?

options.text: It can go anywhere in the circuit

explanation: The current must flow through the ammeter to be measured, so it goes in series, in the path of the current. An ammeter has almost no resistance, so across a part it would let the current bypass that part.

prompt: Why is a voltmeter connected across a resistor, not in series with it?

options.text: It must carry all the current in the circuit
It measures the potential difference between the two ends of the resistor

explanation: A voltmeter compares the two ends of a part, so it is joined to both ends. It has a very high resistance, so in series it would stop almost all of the current.
